$comment: A derived template (packs/README.md 'Derived templates'): the care pack composed with a fertility clinic's content seed, re-registered in the fogline register (white ground, plum ink, dusty rose) with its own pinned page skeletons. Everything else — pages' builders, sections, contract, tests — is the base pack's; compose expands this catalog through resolveCatalog (scripts/lib/pack-switch.mjs).
title: Fertility Clinic
description: A fertility clinic's site with real online booking: Clearwater Fertility in San Francisco, built around telling patients the odds plainly. The home opens on a couple on a bench above the city in the fog under "The honest path to a family.", then the numbers as a report — live-birth rates per retrieval by age band, each row with its bar, the footnote, and a visible sample-data tag until the owner enters the clinic's own reported rates — and the prices over the consultation ask. The team, treatments with their prices, the benefits billed directly, and a booking widget for consultations, intro calls, and follow-ups keep their own pages. White, plum, and dusty rose in a narrow modern serif. Flexes to IVF and egg-freezing clinics, reproductive urology, and any practice that publishes outcomes.

content.$comment: Business-content contract seed override. resolveCatalog merges a remix's content per-domain over the base's, so these practice and appointments seeds replace the base pack's at compose and mirror THIS remix's contentSeed module entry for entry (the remix-seed tests pin the twins) — the composed template's Manage editors and booking widget open on the fertility clinic, not the base clinic.

providers.name: Meera Rao
providers.bio: Dr. Rao trained at UCSF and opened Clearwater in 2016 to run a clinic that tells patients the odds plainly. She sees every new patient at least once, and she will draw your timeline on paper until it makes sense.

providers.name: Daniel Moreno
providers.bio: Dr. Moreno leads the egg-freezing and donor programs and works with many LGBTQ+ families building through donors and gestational carriers. He's bilingual in English and Spanish and answers his own messages.

providers.name: Grace Lin
providers.bio: Grace is the person you'll talk to most: medication calendars, monitoring times, the 6 a.m. question. She has coordinated more than two thousand cycles and still celebrates every call with good news.

services.name: Fertility consultation
services.description: An hour with a physician: your history, your tests, and a plain account of your options and odds — including doing nothing yet.

services.name: IVF
services.description: Stimulation, retrieval, and transfer, with monitoring before work and a nurse coordinator who knows your calendar.

services.name: Egg freezing
services.description: One or two cycles, with a straight answer about how many eggs you're likely to need at your age.

services.name: IUI
services.description: A simpler first step for some couples and single parents, with or without medication.

services.name: Fertility testing
services.description: Bloodwork, ultrasound, and semen analysis in one morning, with results explained at a follow-up — not in a portal.

services.name: Donor & carrier programs
services.description: Egg and sperm donors and gestational carriers, for LGBTQ+ families, single parents, and anyone who needs them.

locations.label: Clay Street
locations.address: 2340 Clay Street, Suite 400, San Francisco, CA 94115

reviews.quote: Dr. Rao showed us the real numbers at the first visit, and then she showed us what would change them. We knew exactly what we were choosing.
reviews.name: Ana & Chris P.

reviews.quote: Grace texted me back at 6:10 in the morning about a dose. That's the whole review.
reviews.name: Jordan M.

reviews.quote: Dr. Moreno never once made us feel like an exception. Two dads, one donor, one carrier, one very loud daughter.
reviews.name: Sam & Eli T.

newPatient.title: Book a consultation
newPatient.body: Most people see a physician within a week. Bring any old test results; we'll order what's missing.

newPatient.title: Testing in one morning
newPatient.body: Bloodwork, ultrasound, and a semen analysis if it applies, all before ten.

newPatient.title: A plan and a price
newPatient.body: At your follow-up you get a written plan, your odds as we see them, and the cost with and without your benefits.

newPatient.title: Your coordinator
newPatient.body: From then on, Grace or one of her team is your first call for everything.

types.name: New-patient consultation
types.description: An hour with a physician, in person or by video.

types.name: Free intro call
types.description: Fifteen minutes with a nurse coordinator to ask anything first.

types.name: Follow-up
types.description: Results, your plan, and next steps with your physician.

theme.$comment: The fogline register's rose as the project brand: mode light opens the site in the register's native appearance (white ground, plum ink, dusty rose); the Feel toggle swaps to the same room at night. Marketing pages resolve brand over preset accent, so keeping the values identical to the preset's own accents re-inks app surfaces without shifting the pages. The shared careShell's full-width chrome stays — framestack floats it over the home's photograph and inkover sets it in plum over the fog.

landing.$comment: A pinned layout (packs/README.md 'Derived templates'): style re-registers the base's pages in the fogline register, and pages carries exactly the skeletons careLanding.ts emits from this remix's contentSeed — the seed sets home.stack with a report and no band or frames, so the home is the photograph, the numbers (stats bars), and the colophon consultation ask; the inner pages are the base's, with the price list because the seed fills it — so the composed template's document reproduces its code config section for section (tests/View/Care/careLanding.test.ts reads this through composedLandingSeed).
